problem_type: canonical base64 validation of a full multi-megabyte payload with a stack-recursive regex overflows the engine stack
symptom: Certifying a model's media artifact whose source is a multi-megabyte `data:` URL (b64_json video or 3D, e.g. 3.4MB+) threw a raw 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'. The model self-certification failed with an unreadable error and the model stayed enabled:false; the user saw the generic 'this error we did not recognize'. A ~21KB data URL certified normally, so the failure was purely payload-size driven.
direct_cause: strictDataUrl validated the base64 body with `^(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{4})*(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{2}==|[A-Za-z0-9+/]{3}=)?$`. V8's Irregexp compiles a fixed-length group repeated by `*` into a recursive backtracking structure, pushing one native stack frame per 4-character group. A multi-megabyte base64 body has on the order of a million such groups, so RegExp.test overflowed the regex stack before decoding ever began.
class_root: The certification byte-syntax boundary expressed 'is this a canonical base64 body?' as a regex whose stack cost grows with payload length. Every media kind (image/video/audio/model3d) and every producer that hands a `data:` URL to certification flows through this single gate, so any large embedded payload could trip the same recursion. The missing invariant is that full-payload base64 syntax validation must run in bounded stack space (a linear scan), independent of length.
affected_population: Any model whose vendor returns a media artifact as an inline base64 `data:` URL (b64_json) above roughly a few hundred KB — confirmed for video and 3D (GLB) payloads

All four production callers of certification: adapter self-verification (verifier.verifyAdapterMode), task-output certification (taskResultCertification.certifyTaskOutputUrls), and the ComfyUI connector/candidate lifecycle
Future certification callers passing large inline data URLs for image or audio kinds
entry_points: Task output certification (certifyTaskOutputUrls → certifyMediaArtifact) for image/video/audio/model3d
ComfyUI connector and candidate lifecycle certification (comfyuiConnector / comfyuiCandidateLifecycle → certifyMediaArtifact / certifyTaskOutputUrls)
internal_only_reason: The canonical base64 grammar and its stack-safe recognition are Nomi's own certification byte-boundary invariant; no external provider or specification dictates the validation implementation. Equivalence to the standard base64 grammar was proven against the prior regex, not read from a third-party doc.
invariants: Full-payload base64 syntax validation runs in bounded stack space (a linear character scan), so payload length can never overflow the regex/engine stack.

The syntax check accepts exactly the canonical standard-alphabet base64 grammar it replaced: length a multiple of 4, characters in [A-Za-z0-9+/], and '=' padding only as the final one or two characters.
An over-limit base64 payload fails as media_too_large before the syntax scan and before any decode; an invalid-but-in-limit payload fails as media_invalid_source. Neither surfaces a stack-overflow.
The empty body remains canonical at the syntax layer; non-empty bytes are enforced separately after decoding, preserving prior behavior.
generality_proof: Every certification caller converges on certifyMediaArtifact → acquireBytes → strictDataUrl, which is now the only path that validates an inline base64 body and does so exclusively through electron/providerAdapter/base64.ts isCanonicalBase64Body. That helper is a linear scan with no quantified-group recursion, so the bounded-stack invariant holds for every media kind and every producer regardless of payload size. A repository scan confirmed strictDataUrl held the only grouped-repeat-in-star base64 regex; the remaining base64 gates use flat character-class quantifiers, which V8 compiles to non-recursive loops and which were shown not to overflow on the same 5.4MB payload.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the single, stack-safe recognizer for canonical standard-alphabet base64 bodies; any certification/boundary layer that must judge base64 syntax calls this instead of hand-rolling a length-recursive regex.

Enforce the size limit before syntax, then validate the base64 body only through isCanonicalBase64Body, so large inline data URLs fail with an honest reason code or certify, never with a stack overflow.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: certifyMedia defaults to certifyMediaArtifact, whose only inline-base64 path is strictDataUrl; the model-certification flow that produced the reported symptom now runs the linear scan.
Maps every source URL through certifyMediaArtifact, so any large b64_json data URL from any vendor is validated by isCanonicalBase64Body at the shared boundary.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: decodeBase64 / strictImageDataUri (embedded GLB buffers and images)
same_class_entry_points.evidence: These decode embedded base64 via a flat character-class regex plus a length%4/maxBytes guard and Uint8Array.from(atob(...), fn) (iterator, no spread). Empirically the flat regex does not overflow on a 5.4MB payload, and the length guard bounds atob input; they are outside the grouped-repeat class.

recurrence.reason: The same certification gate is reached by four distinct production callers carrying different media kinds and vendor payload shapes, and any of them with a large inline data URL hit the identical mechanism. The structural anti-pattern (a length-recursive base64 regex) can also reappear if a future gate re-implements base64 syntax by hand, so the invariant must live behind one shared recognizer.
same_class_scan: grep -rnE '\(\?:[^)]*\{[0-9]+\}[^)]*\)\*' over electron/ and src/ returned only certificationMedia.ts:267 as a grouped-repeat-in-star regex; no other production site shares the recursion.

Empirically ran each base64 validation regex (certificationMedia:267, synchronousAudioResponse:47, antigravityTask:23, model3dValidation:62/98, assetUrlExtract:99) against the real 5.4MB fixture-derived base64: only the grouped `(?:...{4})*` pattern threw 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'; the flat character-class patterns did not.

Confirmed the String.fromCharCode(...subarray) and ascii() call sites in mediaTypes.ts and model3dValidation.ts are all bounded to 4-byte (<=4096 for ftyp box) literal windows, so the spread family is not on the large-payload path.

Enumerated the four certification callers (verifier, taskResultCertification, comfyuiConnector, comfyuiCandidateLifecycle) and confirmed each converges on certifyMediaArtifact → strictDataUrl for inline data URLs.

prevention.invariant: Canonical base64 body recognition is performed only by isCanonicalBase64Body, a linear scan whose stack cost is O(1) in payload length.
prevention.failure_mode: Over-limit payloads fail as media_too_large before the scan; malformed in-limit payloads fail as media_invalid_source; no input path can produce a stack overflow.
prevention.strategy: Replace the length-recursive regex with a single shared, non-recursive recognizer and route the certification byte-syntax gate through it, so every caller and future gate inherits the bounded-stack invariant instead of re-deriving a regex.

legacy_paths.rationale: The stack-recursive `(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{4})*(?:...)?` regex in strictDataUrl is deleted in the same change and replaced by the shared isCanonicalBase64Body call; no fallback to the old regex remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The defect is in Nomi's own validation code, not a third-party runtime. V8's regex engine behaves correctly; the fix removes the pathological pattern rather than changing any dependency.

migration: No data or state migration. Behavior for previously accepted small data URLs is unchanged (the recognizer is grammar-equivalent to the prior regex). Previously crashing large payloads now certify when valid and within limit, or fail with an honest reason code when not.
residual_risks: Certification decode of a genuinely large valid video still relies on the bundled ffmpeg/ffprobe within the decoder timeout; a real >limit valid video is rejected by size before decode, which is the intended honest failure and not covered by an end-to-end paid generation here.
